title: What Pairwise Evaluation Misses: Reward Scores across Prompts
abstract: arXiv:2610.31090v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Reward models score responses for preference optimization, filtering and ranking, and pooling scores across prompts needs them to be comparable. Yet pairwise evaluation compares two responses to the same prompt, so any score component shared by a prompt's responses cancels and goes untested. We study this component by comparing between-prompt variation in model scores with the same variation in human ratings of the same responses. We propose a human-referenced audit, built from a between-prompt variance share, a sibling-rating regression and prompt substitutions, and apply it to eighteen released scorers and six matched training conditions. We find that scores cluster by prompt more than the ratings do: on HelpSteer2, six reward models have between-prompt shares of 0.34 to 0.64 against a human share near zero. Replacing the original prompt with a fixed instruction keeps substantial clustering but weakens agreement with prompt-level human

translated_title: 成对评估所遗漏的：跨提示的奖励分数
translated_abstract: 奖励模型为偏好优化、过滤和排序对响应进行评分，而跨提示汇总分数要求这些分数具有可比性。然而，成对评估比较的是同一提示下的两个响应，因此某个提示的所有响应所共享的任何分数成分都会被抵消，从而无法被检验。我们通过比较模型分数在提示之间的变异与人类对相同响应评分的相应变异来研究这一成分。我们提出了一种以人类为参照的审计方法，该方法由提示间方差份额、同胞评分回归和提示替换构成，并将其应用于十八个已发布的评分器和六个匹配的训练条件。我们发现分数按提示聚集的程度高于人类评分：在 HelpSteer2 上，六个奖励模型的提示间份额为 0.34 至 0.64，而人类评分的份额接近于零。用固定指令替换原始提示后，大量的聚集性依然存在，但与提示级人类评分的一致性被削弱。
tldr: 论文提出一种以人类评分为参照的审计方法，揭示奖励模型分数存在按提示聚集的跨提示不可比成分——这是成对评估无法检测到的，六个奖励模型的提示间方差份额高达0.34-0.64，而人类评分接近于零。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes a human-referenced audit revealing that reward model scores cluster by prompt—a cross-prompt incomparability component that pairwise evaluation fails to test—with between-prompt variance shares of 0.34-0.64 for six reward models versus near-zero for human ratings.
